questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer: To destroy all means of retreat and commit irrevocably

Explanation:

  • To end a journey prematurely ❌ → Incorrect; it’s about cutting off retreat, not stopping early.

Diego Simeone ate his own words when Cristiano Ronaldo scored three goals and defeated Atletico Madrid.

options.label: B
options.text: retracted what he had said before

questions.solution:
Ate his own words: retract what one has said, especially in a humiliating way.

The rest of the meanings are contextually incorrect.

questions.question:
Complete the dialogue for Person B using the correct idiom.

Person A: That startup failed fast, didn't it?

Person B: Yeah, it was clearly a case of _____.

options.label: A
options.text: putting the cart before the ox

options.label: B
options.text: placing the cart ahead of the horse

options.label: C
options.text: putting the cart before the horse

options.label: D
options.text: pulling the cart with the horse

questions.solution:
The idiom "putting the cart before the horse" means doing things in the wrong order or getting priorities mixed up. In this context, the startup failed because it likely focused on the wrong steps first, so the idiom fits perfectly.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Other options are not appropriate idioms.

The majestic whale glided through the ocean depths, symbolising the inspiring wonders of marine life.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

That politician always ______ to avoid giving a clear answer.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank is: b) beats around the bush.

"Beat around the bush" means to avoid talking directly about the main topic or to be evasive - exactly what the sentence describes: a politician avoiding a clear answer.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Bites the bullet: Means to endure a painful or unpleasant situation bravely. This doesn't fit the idea of avoidance.

Throws in the towel: Means to give up or surrender, usually in the face of difficulty - unrelated to being evasive.

Hits the ground running: Means to begin a task with energy and enthusiasm - again, not relevant to the context of dodging questions.

Choose the word which is nearest in meaning to the highlighted word.

The defense attorney's trenchant arguments quickly turned the tide of the trial in favor of the accused.
questions.question_hi:
Choose the word which is nearest in meaning to the highlighted word.

The defense attorney's trenchant arguments quickly turned the tide of the trial in favor of the accused.
questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer: Sharp (तेज़ / तीक्ष्ण)

Explanation:

Sentence: The defense attorney's trenchant arguments quickly turned the tide of the trial in favor of the accused.

  • Trenchant (तीक्ष्ण / धारदार) → Means keen, incisive, forceful, sharp in expression or style.
  • Here, the attorney’s arguments were clear, cutting, and effective, so “Sharp (तेज़ / तीक्ष्ण)” is the nearest synonym.

Why Other Options Are Wrong

  • Vague (अस्पष्ट) ❌ → Opposite of trenchant; unclear.
  • Aggressive (आक्रामक) ❌ → Trenchant can be forceful, but it emphasizes clarity and sharpness, not hostility.
  • Tedious (नीरस / उबाऊ) ❌ → Means boring or monotonous, opposite of trenchant.
